title: Albert McCormick Community Centre renovation funding and contract
subtitle: 2024 surplus allocation, pumping station grant bid, and a six-storey Albert Street development approved
overview: Council awarded the Phase A construction contract for the Albert McCormick Community Centre energy and accessibility retrofit {{vote:m8}}. The work covers rink cooling, a new roof, electrified heating and new accessible washrooms and change rooms. Construction is planned to start at the end of May and finish by March 2026. Council also endorsed the Phase B renovation and library expansion {{vote:m9}}. Staff must return with a funding strategy before the project is tendered, because a large shortfall remains.

Council allocated the 2024 property-tax surplus to reserves, including the planning litigation, cemetery, tax rate stabilization, infrastructure, climate action and library reserves {{vote:m10}}. It approved a Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund application for two sanitary pumping stations in Beaver Creek Meadows {{vote:m11}}.

At an evening public meeting, council approved an Official Plan and zoning amendment for a six-storey mixed-use building on Albert and Hemlock Streets in Northdale {{vote:m12}}. Council also received several financial reports on consent, and the mayor said staff expect a report in June on a temporary leash-free dog park in Uptown.

decisions.detail: Council awarded RFT25-10 to Zehr Construction Inc. for a total of $4,979,718.20 including unrecoverable HST, released $1,500,000 in capital funding and approved $788,000 in transfers from other projects.

decisions.item: AMCC Phase B and library expansion
decisions.detail: Council approved the project update, directed staff to return with a funding strategy for the full revised scope before tendering, and to include Phase B in the Development Charge Background Study update.
Council acknowledged a $2,659,662 surplus, put $500,000 into the Planning Litigation Reserve Fund and $250,000 into the Cemetery Reserve Fund, and split the remaining $1,909,662 among four reserves.

decisions.item: Beaver Creek Meadows pumping stations grant
decisions.detail: Council approved a Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund application for two sanitary pumping stations, with the fund covering up to $8,429,000 of a $21,073,000 cost, and set out next steps whether or not the application succeeds.
Council approved Official Plan Amendment No. 57 and Zoning By-law Amendment Z-24-12 for 310, 330 and 332 Albert Street and 291, 293 and 295 Hemlock Street.

decisions.item: Signing authority for 460 Columbia Street West
decisions.detail: Council authorized the Director of Planning to sign documents and the final plan for the condominium at 460 Columbia Street West.

debate: Councillors asked how Phase A construction would affect user groups. Staff said only one rink would close at a time over the summer, with ice back by September and washroom work finishing around mid-October. A councillor suggested involving user groups early because the new universal change room is far from the other dressing rooms and might go unused.

On Phase B, a councillor questioned the engagement behind the design. Staff said they leaned on earlier engagement and the library's own consultation, and would hold more focused public engagement and in-neighbourhood sessions after approval.

Council pressed on how to close the roughly $7 million funding gap and which parts of the design could be deferred. Library board representatives and staff said they saw nothing that could be dropped. Staff listed options including development charges, grants, reserves, land sale proceeds or deferral to the 2027 capital budget, and said tariff uncertainty could change costs.
Council members and the mayor again called for a new municipal funding formula and for projects that are ready if stimulus money arrives.

On the Albert Street development, councillors asked about the Hemlock Street frontage and tree replacement. Staff said grades prevent a direct street-level unit entrance and that tree compensation would be settled at site plan, possibly off-site or as payment. A councillor also raised parking disputes in Northdale. The applicant's planner said parking would be leased separately from units, with passes and enforcement through building management.
